blocks.x: Meter-data lakehouse with billing-grade quality, billing exceptions down 63% and non-technical loss analytics finally trustworthy
Identity withheld, a city utility whose meters spoke daily and whose billing listened roughly once a month. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter read the noise: 14% of billing runs carrying exceptions resolved by manual estimate, non-technical-loss analytics distrusted because meter data quality was unknown, and revenue protection blocked by its own evidence problem.
The meter estate was heterogeneous, three AMI generations and a decade of manual reads, and no layer existed that made any of it billing-grade.

We built the meter-data lakehouse as the trust layer: ingestion normalizing three AMI generations plus manual reads into one validated model, quality scoring per meter with repair feeds to the field, billing consuming validated reads with exception rates reported per run, and loss analytics running on data the field has confirmed. Estimates became exceptions, not defaults.
